question: Which of the following element has maximum density?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Osmium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Osmium is a dense metal belonging to the platinum group and has the highest density of any naturally occurring element.
 
• Its density is approximately 22.59 grams per cubic centimeter, making it the densest natural element.
 
• Osmium is used in alloys with other platinum-group metals to produce extremely hard materials for specialized applications.
 
• It is a hard, brittle metal with a bluish tint and is typically found in nature as an alloy with other platinum group metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Density:** Density is defined as the mass per unit volume of a substance. It is typically expressed in grams per cubic centimeter (g/cm³). The formula for density is:

 
 
• Density = Mass / Volume
 
 
 
• **Platinum Group Metals (PGM):** These are six metallic elements clustered together in the periodic table. They are platinum (Pt), palladium (Pd), rhodium (Rh), ruthenium (Ru), iridium (Ir), and osmium (Os). These metals have similar physical and chemical properties and tend to occur together in the same mineral deposits.
 
• **Applications of Osmium:**
 
 
• Osmium is used in fountain pen tips, electrical contacts, and in other applications where extreme durability and hardness are needed.
 
• Osmium tetroxide, a compound of osmium, is used in staining tissues in electron microscopy.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Elements:**
 
 
• Lead has a density of approximately 11.34 g/cm³, which is significantly lower than osmium.
 
• Platinum has a density of around 21.45 g/cm³, which is also lower than osmium but still very high.
 
• Mercury has a density of approximately 13.53 g/cm³.
